reason: While the text shows Yahweh offering a good land ('flowing with milk and honey') to the Israelites, the overwhelming narrative focus of this passage is on divine judgment and punishment for faithlessness. When the people respond to the scouts' report with fear and demand to return to Egypt, Yahweh's response is not protective care but severe judgment: He declares the entire generation (except Caleb and Joshua) will die in the wilderness, and that the people will wander for 40 years. The passage emphasizes Yahweh's anger at their disbelief ('How long will this evil community grumble against me?'), His justice, and His enforcement of consequences for rebellion. The conditional nature of His blessings (contingent on faith and obedience) and the harshness of the punishment contradict a reading that 'Yahweh wants the Hebrew people to be well.' Rather, the text demonstrates that Yahweh prioritizes covenant faithfulness and obedience, and will judge those who reject His promises.
